title: Proportional and Non-Proportional Relationships
seo_title: Grade 8 Proportional and Non-Proportional Relationships Worksheets (TEKS 8.5F, STAAR)
standard_text: 8.4B graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the line that models the relationship; 8.5A represent linear proportional situations with tables, graphs, and equations in the form of y = kx; 8.5B represent linear non-proportional situations with tables, graphs, and equations in the form of y = mx + b, where b ≠ 0; 8.5E solve problems involving direct variation; 8.5F distinguish between proportional and non-proportional situations using tables, graphs, and equations in the form y = kx or y = mx + b, where b ≠ 0
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 worksheets for Texas TEKS 8.4B and 8.5: proportional and non-proportional relationships in tables, equations and situations, direct variation and unit rate as slope. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Proportional: y = kx through (0, 0). Non-proportional: y = mx + b, b ≠ 0.
key_sub: A starting fee makes a relationship non-proportional.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A proportional relationship has the form y = kx. Its graph is a straight line through (0, 0), and y ÷ x is the same for every pair.
  • A non-proportional linear relationship has the form y = mx + b with b ≠ 0. Its graph does not pass through (0, 0).
  • In a proportional graph, the unit rate is the slope.
  • Direct variation means y = kx: find k = y ÷ x, then use it.

Examples

Example

$25 fee plus $10 per hour

Starts at 25, not 0

Answer: non-proportional: y = 10x + 25

Example

y varies directly with x; y = 18 when x = 3. Find y when x = 7.

k = 6

6 × 7

Answer: 42

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling every straight line proportionalIt must also pass through (0, 0).
Checking only one pairEvery pair must have the same y ÷ x.
Forgetting a starting amountA fee or starting value makes it non-proportional.

sets.title: The unit rate as the slope

items.q:
x0124
y03612
A printer prints pages. The table is a proportional relationship. What is the slope (the unit rate)?
items.e: The line goes through (0, 0). Slope = y ÷ x = 3 ÷ 1 = 3 pages per minute.

items.q: Which equation shows a proportional relationship?
items.e: A proportional relationship goes through (0, 0): y = kx with no + b. The answer is y = 4x.

Water fills a tank. The table is a proportional relationship. What is the slope (the unit rate)?
items.e: The line goes through (0, 0). Slope = y ÷ x = 52 ÷ 1 = 52 gallons per minute.

items.q: The graph shows a proportional relationship. What is the unit rate?
items.e: Find the point (1, 2). Unit rate = slope = 2 ÷ 1 = 2.

items.q: A line goes through (0, 0) and (5, 20). Which is true?
c: It is proportional with unit rate 4
It is proportional with unit rate 5
items.e: It goes through the origin and slope = 20 ÷ 5 = 4. It is proportional with unit rate 4.
